=== CONSULTING BRIEF (every field below is mandatory grounding for the prototype) ===
Thesis: An AI-brokered marketplace in Teams that matches first-years with 2-week, low-risk project sprints sponsored by Microsoft and other partners.
Description (what gets built):
University policy rigidly defines co-ops as 6-month engagements, locking first-year undergraduate students out of formal experience. This tool leverages the new Microsoft AI Innovation Lab partnership. It uses an AI agent to break down larger industry problems into 2-week 'micro-projects'. It then matches these micro-projects to first-year undergraduate students via Teams based on their current coursework. Students gain verifiable resume experience, partners get lightweight tasks completed, and the university bypasses the rigid policy constraints of formal co-op.
Why it matters for first-year undergraduate students:
First-year undergraduate students are desperate for resume-building experiences but are institutionally barred from formal co-op. By providing micro-projects, first-year undergraduate students can build a track record of success early, making them significantly more competitive when they finally enter the formal co-op market.
How it supports first-year undergraduate students outcomes over first 18-24 months:
Completing 2-3 micro-projects in the first 18-24 months provides concrete evidence of reliability and skill. This dramatically improves their match rate for year-three co-ops and aligns perfectly with Chris's mandate to push experiential opportunities into the first year.
Execution within Northeastern University's existing stack (named systems, connectors, AI layer location):
Operates entirely within Microsoft Teams and SharePoint. Leverages the existing project-based industry pipeline infrastructure Ben is managing.
Microsoft 365 Copilot, Teams, SharePoint, Power Automate, Power BI, Azure OpenAI fit (named tools that reduce cost/burden):
Capitalizes directly on the incoming Microsoft partnership (co-branded badges, project clearinghouse) and utilizes Teams for the matching and execution.
Key stakeholders:
  1. Ben — Owns the project-based industry partnerships.
  2. Jen — Manages the Microsoft tenant and security boundaries for external partner access.
  3. Kelly Anne — Ensures micro-projects do not conflict with formal co-op policy definitions.
Implementation steps (the prototype should visibly demonstrate at least one of these in action):
  Step 1: Secure 5 pilot micro-projects from Microsoft/Verizon (owner: Ben, effort: 3 weeks)
  Step 2: Configure Teams matching bot using Azure OpenAI (owner: Jen, effort: 3 weeks, deps: Project inventory)
  Step 3: Establish sandboxed MSFT environments for student work (owner: Jen, effort: 2 weeks, deps: Teams bot)
  Step 4: Launch pilot to Khoury first-years (owner: Ben, effort: 1 week, deps: Sandboxed environments)
Risks & mitigations (surface relevant risks as in-product safeguards or copy):
  1. [HIGH] Policy group (Kelly Anne) shuts it down as unregulated work → Strictly brand as 'academic projects' or 'micro-internships', completely divorced from the word 'co-op'.
  2. [MEDIUM] Quality control of student output → Require a peer-review step before submitting to the industry partner.
  3. [HIGH] Data security with corporate IP → All work occurs in heavily locked-down, Northeastern-managed Azure sandboxes.
Guardrail fit (why this passes the Liz Zulick & Jen & Chris meeting filter — preserve this rationale visually in the prototype):
Directly supports Ben's industry-project pipeline. Honors Chris's desire for first-year experience. Uses the Microsoft stack to reduce cost and leverage the new LOI.

Generate 200 micro-project completions in year one; participants see a 30% increase in first-round co-op interview rates.

The "aha" interaction (the single moment the user feels the product working): Accepting a 10-hour 'Data Cleaning Sprint' for a Verizon project directly inside Microsoft Teams, resulting in a verified badge.

=== GROUNDING THEMES (cited by this concept) ===
  1. AI-Driven First-Year Readiness Interventions
    Thesis: Students are arriving at the university increasingly unprepared for the rigorous co-op search process, lacking foundational resume and interview skills. To combat this, institutions are deploying AI-enabled readiness roadmaps that ingest admissions data to baseline skills before formal human advising begins. This early intervention shifts the burden of basic career reflection away from 1:1 advisor meetings.

  2. Stealth Implementation of Comprehensive Learner Record
    Thesis: Past failures with large-scale platforms, specifically the Student Assessed Integrated Learning (SAIL) initiative, have created institutional resistance to comprehensive system pitches. Leadership advises that new AI and CLR initiatives must be framed as bite-sized, tactical interventions. By embedding data collection quietly within high-utility first-year readiness tools, the university can build comprehensive learner profiles without triggering executive scrutiny.

  3. System Fragmentation and Shadow IT Workarounds
    Thesis: The student digital ecosystem is highly fragmented, requiring users to navigate up to 20 disconnected systems from initial search through matriculation. This lack of a unified platform forces students to engineer their own shadow IT workarounds, such as personal spreadsheets, to track co-op applications. Consequently, the university loses critical data visibility into the co-op pipeline.

=== RESEARCH GOAL (the engagement question this prototype helps answer) ===
Identify a comprehensive new strategy for co-op based on the current statement of work for NU, prior projects with NU, and fresh industry analysis of experiential learning and co-op engagement tactics to improve learner's chances of gaining meaningful experiential learning opportunities from pre-enrollment to graduate school
=== BUILD INSTRUCTIONS ===
Think ultra hard about the persona's actual pain points above. Build a multi-screen experience that:
  1. Opens in a state reflecting the persona's actual emotional/situational reality (not a generic "welcome"). Reference their context from the FULL PERSONA PROFILE.
  2. Demonstrates the implementation steps from the BRIEF as live, working interactions — at least 1-2 of those steps should be a screen the user navigates to and an AI flow they fire.
  3. Uses verbatim quotes from the THEMES / verbatim_quote_evidence block as in-product evidence/testimonials — NEVER lorem ipsum.
  4. References the persona by their real name throughout. Names from the uploads should appear in seed data (real co-op partners, real programs).
  5. Demonstrates the "aha" interaction explicitly as one screen-or-state with the AI call wired LIVE to /api/ai/gemini-compat (or /api/ai/anthropic, /api/wiki/fetch-articles depending on capability).
  6. Surfaces the expected_impact metrics as visible KPI badges where natural.
  7. Honors every guardrail in guardrail_fit — visibly. If "no new platform" is in the guardrails, the prototype's chrome should communicate "this lives inside [existing system]" (e.g., a Copilot Studio badge in the header).

brief.frame_rationale: The concept explicitly requested a NON_OBVIOUS_BET. Instead of building a destination job board (which risks feeling like a new platform), this frame embeds the experience directly into the student's existing Microsoft Teams classroom environment, using passive skill extraction (referencing Daniel Seaton's real initiative) to proactively route decomposed micro-projects without any application process.
brief.one_line_thesis: An AI-brokered Teams marketplace matching first-years to 2-week, low-risk industry sprints based on passive coursework analysis.

primary_persona.name: Maya
primary_persona.context: Ambitious first-year undergraduate student at Northeastern (Khoury College). She is desperate for resume-building experiences but is institutionally barred from formal co-op by the strict 6-month policy.
primary_persona.emotional_state: Frustrated by the catch-22 of needing experience to get experience, but eager to prove herself if given a bite-sized opportunity.

secondary_actors.involvement: Secures the pilot micro-projects from Microsoft/Verizon and acts as the 'sender' of the opportunities in Teams.
Her policies are visibly enforced via the locked-down Azure sandboxes where the student work occurs.
Invisible but satisfied stakeholder; the UI strictly brands these as 'Academic Projects' to avoid triggering her co-op policy shutdown.

brief.demonstrated_moment: Maya is in her CS2500 Teams channel. After submitting an assignment, the NU Academic Projects Copilot passively extracts her skills and proactively offers her a 10-hour 'Data Cleaning Sprint' for Verizon. She accepts it in one click, instantly provisioning a secure Azure workspace. This answers the research goal: how to improve early experiential learning without violating policy.
jobs_to_be_done: Bypass rigid 6-month co-op policies to gain verifiable industry experience in year one.
Translate my current academic coursework into matched industry micro-tasks without filling out forms or resumes (zero manual data entry).
Complete bite-sized (10-hour) projects in a secure, university-approved environment that protects my data and the sponsor's IP.
Build a track record of success (badges) to improve my match rate for year-three formal co-ops.
success_criteria: Feels differentiated from generic SaaS by living entirely within the chrome of Microsoft Teams as a native Copilot interaction.
Demonstrates zero manual data entry for the student; the system infers readiness based on Daniel Seaton's curriculum skill extraction.
Visibly honors the 'no scoring or shaming' constraint by only surfacing positive, unlocked opportunities (no red metrics, no 'unqualified' states).
Clearly brands the work as 'Academic Projects' or 'Micro-Internships' to bypass policy constraints.

Integrates the verbatim quote as an educational tooltip or onboarding context from Ben: 'Policy is rigid and is itself a constraint on innovation... Co-ops must be six months and at least 55 days. That is why we built Micro-Sprints.'

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the core Teams-embedded experience, honors the non-obvious bet, and wires all three required AI flows to real endpoints. However, it introduces several rogue colors, non-compliant spacing values, and rogue typography sizes that violate the strict Design System. It also lacks standard React and Lucide imports required for runnability.

issues.description: Missing standard imports for React, Framer Motion, and Lucide icons, which will cause the prototype to crash in a standard environment.
issues.fix: Add explicit imports for React, framer-motion, and lucide-react.

issues.description: Introduction of rogue colors not defined in the Design System (e.g., #737373, #F0F0F0, #FBE7EA, and various hex codes in the Jupyter mock).
issues.code_location: CSS Variables and inline styles throughout
issues.fix: Replace all rogue hex codes with strict mappings to the provided semantic and foundation color tokens (e.g., var(--text-secondary), var(--surface-color)).

issues.description: Use of spacing values outside the defined scale (e.g., 12px, 20px, 60px).
issues.fix: Snap all spacing and structural dimensions to the allowed scale: [4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96].

issues.description: Use of font sizes outside the defined typography system (e.g., 32px, 20px, 13px, 12px, 10px).
issues.fix: Snap all font sizes to the allowed values: 48px (display), 24px (quote), 16px (body), 14px (label/data).
